top3_ordered_templates.activity_chain: Observe in order: first {first_action}; then {second_action}; finally {third_action}.
top3_ordered_templates.core_reading: These three leading interest dimensions indicate that {labels} activities stand relatively high in this response. {code} only sets a reading order: {first_label} is the initial observation entry point, with {second_label} and {third_label} as additional entry points. It cannot establish a personality identity, ability level, or career conclusion.
top3_ordered_templates.positive_value: The value of this content is to break the clues into observable small tasks: {first_label} focuses on {first_focus}; {second_label} focuses on {second_focus}; {third_label} focuses on {third_focus}. Whichever comes first only indicates which activity to gather evidence from first. These clues offer exploration questions, not job answers.
top3_ordered_templates.first_experiment: Spend 30 minutes on a low-risk observation: first include an activity involving {first_short}, then one involving {second_short}, and finally one involving {third_short}. Record only which part you most want to continue.
top3_ordered_templates.ordered_code_handling: {code} is the ordered three-letter code for this assessment: the first dimension, {first_label}, is the initial observation entry point; the second, {second_label}, and the third, {third_label}, are additional entry points. The order changes what to ask first and what to explore next. It is not a fixed identity, an ability conclusion, or a career answer.
top3_ordered_templates.low_risk_validation: Low-risk observation: choose a small task that accommodates {first_short}, {second_short}, and {third_short} clues. Record the three activities separately and look only at activity preferences and evidence of wanting to continue.
top3_ordered_templates.primary_activity_chain: Start with the first dimension, {first_label}: use it as the initial observation entry point and look for small-task evidence involving {first_focus}.
top3_ordered_templates.secondary_support_line: Then consider the second dimension, {second_label}: use it as an additional observation entry point and record whether {second_focus} make the task more appealing.
top3_ordered_templates.tertiary_stabilizer: The third dimension, {third_label}, is only an additional clue: observe whether {third_focus} help distinguish more specific task conditions.
top3_ordered_templates.free_page_teaser: The {labels} interest clues can be observed in the order {code} without rushing to a career answer.

task_activity_card.title: Task activity card
task_activity_card.question: Which work activities do you actually enjoy?
task_activity_card.summary: This card breaks interests down into more specific task activities, helping distinguish interest in the problem itself from the image suggested by a job title.

role_responsibility_card.question: Which responsibilities are you willing to take on at work?
role_responsibility_card.summary: Enjoying a task does not mean enjoying the responsibilities of the job that contains it. This card helps you consider whether you want to define problems, express answers, support understanding, move implementation forward, or maintain processes.

140q_cta.title: Do you enjoy the task itself, or the actual day-to-day work?
140q_cta.summary: 60Q has already provided the interest structure for this response. 140Q only separates observation into tasks, environments, and role responsibilities, offering more clues about day-to-day work. It is not a version for correcting this result, and it does not repair, overturn, or override 60Q.

user_not_wrong_message.title: You can disagree with this result
user_not_wrong_message.summary: You can disagree with this result. Check response quality, close scores, and the activities you pictured while answering. You may record your own observations in the optional trial notes; this page does not use that text to change the measured result.

feedback_no_mutation_boundary.title: Feedback does not change scores
feedback_no_mutation_boundary.summary: Disagreeing, adding favorites, making exclusions, and providing feedback from experiments do not change assessment results, report snapshots, default shared content, or PDF content.

next_step.title: Next step
next_step.summary: First check response quality and close scores. Then choose whether to retake when ready or try a small activity. You may write a preferred direction in your own notes and copy it before leaving; those notes stay only in this page’s memory.

intro.title: Consider the directions you already wanted to explore alongside your result
intro.summary: You can note down careers, majors, courses, projects, or work settings. These are used only to generate exploration questions and do not contribute to assessment scores.

input_boundary.title: Input boundaries
input_boundary.summary: Aspirations are your own material for exploration, not assessment answers. You can use your notes to compare activities in a direction with your current interest clues and list real-world conditions to check. This page does not automatically score or match a target occupation.

no_score_mutation_boundary.title: No changes to assessment results
no_score_mutation_boundary.summary: Aspirations will not override the Holland code measured in this assessment. They will not change RIASEC scores, the report snapshot, shared content, or PDF content.

boundaries.disagree: Disagreeing with the result only affects the exploration path; it does not change the Holland code or RIASEC scores measured in this assessment, the report snapshot, shared content, or the PDF.
boundaries.aspirations: Aspirations serve only to refine exploration questions. They do not override the Holland code measured in this assessment, change RIASEC scores, or establish a career conclusion.
